muLooper.notes: The EOC jack is named End-Of-The-Record-Cycle, but the code writes it only while a recording is running: it goes to 10V when the buffer fills and holds there until the next recording starts. The Dry/Wet input's port name is spelled "Dry/Wet modulatiob" in the source.
lines: Records up to 65536 samples of a signal, splits the recording into chunks and plays one chunk back with feedback overdubbing and a dry and wet mix
Starts filling the buffer with the incoming signal, and releases itself once 65536 samples have been written
A voltage above 0V starts filling the buffer with the incoming signal
Divides the 65536-sample buffer into 1 to 16 chunks, each of them 65536 divided by that number of samples long
Sets the number of chunks the buffer is divided into, 0-10V covering 1 to 16, and overrides the SPLT knob
Picks which chunk plays, 0 at the first and 1 at the last, fading from one chunk to the next in between
Attenuates and inverts the voltage at the SCN input before it is added to the chunk selection
A voltage moving the chunk selection, scaled by the slider for SCN, with 10V covering the whole set of chunks at the slider's full setting
Sets the playback speed in samples per sample, -4 to 4, with negative values playing the recording backwards
Attenuates and inverts the voltage at the SPD input before it is added to the playback speed
A voltage added to the playback speed, scaled by the slider for SPD, with 5V adding one sample per sample at the slider's full setting
Sets how much of what is playing is mixed into the signal being recorded, 0 to 100%
Attenuates and inverts the voltage at the FBK input before it is added to the feedback amount
A voltage added to the feedback amount, scaled by the slider for FBK, with 10V covering the whole range at the slider's full setting
Crossfades the outputs between the incoming signal and the recording, 0% for the incoming signal alone and 100% for the recording alone
Attenuates and inverts the voltage at the WET input before it is added to the dry and wet mix
A voltage added to the dry and wet mix, scaled by the slider for WET, with 10V covering the whole range at the slider's full setting
The signal written into the buffer, summed to one channel if it is polyphonic, and the dry side of the WET mix
The chunk picked by SCN, mixed with the incoming signal by WET
One chunk per channel, as many channels as SPLT sets, counting up from the chunk picked by SCN, each channel mixed with the incoming signal by WET
Rises to 10V when a recording reaches the end of the buffer and holds there until the next recording starts
Note — the readout gives the number of chunks the buffer is split into and the length of one chunk in samples
Menu — Scale speed divides the playback speed by the number of chunks set by SPLT
Chaotic oscillator built on the logistic map, sweeping the map's coefficient between two settings at an audio rate to make scratching and glitching tones
Sets the frequency at which the map's coefficient is swept between the lambda 1 and lambda 2 settings, 54 semitones either side of 261.63Hz
Attenuates and inverts the voltage at the FRQ input before it is added to the frequency, and at its full setting the oscillator tracks a volt per octave
A voltage raising the sweep frequency, scaled by the slider for FRQ, with one volt doubling the frequency at the slider's full setting
Sets one limit of the coefficient sweep, the knob's 0 to 1 covering coefficient values 0.75 to 1
Attenuates and inverts the voltage at the lambda 1 input before it is added to the lambda 1 setting
A voltage added to the lambda 1 setting, scaled by the slider for lambda 1, with 10V covering the knob's whole range at the slider's full setting
Sets the other limit of the coefficient sweep, the knob's 0 to 1 covering coefficient values 0.75 to 1
Attenuates and inverts the voltage at the lambda 2 input before it is added to the lambda 2 setting
A voltage added to the lambda 2 setting, scaled by the slider for lambda 2, with 10V covering the knob's whole range at the slider's full setting
Sets how far the state falls on each sample between iterations of the map, 0.001 to 1, larger values giving a more mellow tone
Attenuates and inverts the voltage at the delta x input before it is added to the delta x setting
A voltage added to the delta x setting, scaled by the slider for delta x, with 10V covering the knob's whole range at the slider's full setting
The oscillator, -5V to 5V

LFSR8Poly.notes: The eight CV knobs have no names in the source; the panel labels the group V/OCT.
lines: Sequencer running an eight-bit linear feedback shift register, sending the register bits out as polyphonic gates and as one weighted CV
Sets all eight feedback coefficients at once, as a whole number from 0 to 255 read as eight bits
Sets all eight feedback coefficients from a voltage, 0-10V covering 0 to 255, and overrides the COEF knob
Switches one feedback coefficient on or off; the register bits whose coefficient is on are combined to make the bit shifted in
Sets how many of the eight register bits are used, 1 to 8
Sets how many register bits are used from a voltage, 0-10V covering 1 to 8, and overrides the LEN knob
Feeds the inverse of the combined bit back into the register, making it an XNOR register rather than an XOR one
A voltage above 0V makes the register feed back the inverted bit, and moves the NOT button with it
A rising edge shifts the register one place, reading high above 2V and low below 0.1V
Scales what one register bit contributes to the CV output, 0 to 1; the first bit can add 10V and each bit after it half as much
Scales the whole CV output, 10V leaving it at full and 0V collapsing it to nothing
One channel per register bit in use, carrying 10V while that bit is set and the clock is high
One voltage summed from the set register bits, each bit weighted by its own V/OCT knob
Note — a register holding all zeros stays at zero; pressing NOT feeds a 1 into it and starts the sequence again

LFSR16Poly.notes: The last four channels of the matrix CV output come from an expression that compares bits rather than shifting them, so those channels are not a binary reading of the column; the line says so rather than claiming a range it does not hold.
lines: Sequencer running a sixteen-bit linear feedback shift register that can be split into two independently clocked registers, with gate and CV outputs for each
Sets all sixteen feedback coefficients at once, as a whole number from 0 to 65535 read as sixteen bits
Sets all sixteen feedback coefficients from a voltage, 0-10V covering 0 to 65535, and overrides the COEF knob
Switches one feedback coefficient on or off; the register bits whose coefficient is on are combined to make the bit shifted in
Sets how many of the sixteen bits belong to the first register, 0 to 16, the rest forming the second register
Sets how many bits belong to the first register from a voltage, 0-10V covering 0 to 16, and overrides the SPLT knob
Makes the first register feed back the inverted bit, an XNOR rather than an XOR
Makes the second register feed back the inverted bit, an XNOR rather than an XOR
A voltage above 0V makes the first register feed back the inverted bit, and moves the NOT1 button with it
A voltage above 0V makes the second register feed back the inverted bit, and moves the NOT2 button with it
A rising edge shifts the first register one place, reading high above 2V and low below 0.1V
A rising edge shifts the second register one place, reading high above 2V and low below 0.1V
One channel per bit of the first register, carrying 10V while that bit is set
One channel per bit of the second register, carrying 10V while that bit is set
Eight channels taken from the sixteen bits read as a four by four grid: the first four carry 10V when a row holds an odd number of set bits, the last four when a column does
The bits of the first register read as a binary number and scaled to 0-10V
The bits of the second register read as a binary number and scaled to 0-10V
Eight channels from the sixteen bits read as a four by four grid: the first four read a row as a four-bit number scaled to 0-10V, the last four come from a column but not as plain binary
Note — each square light shows one register bit: in the first register a set bit is bright and a clear bit dim, and in the second register a set bit is dark and a clear bit dim

Droplets.notes: Liquid moves between cells only on the ticks when a cell reaches the viscosity threshold: in leakCell the leakage worked out for a cell below the threshold is assigned to a shadowed local and never used, so the smooth seepage the model implies does not happen.
lines: Sequencer modelling liquid running down a leaky pipe of eight cells, moving liquid from cell to cell on each clock tick and firing a gate wherever a cell empties
Sets how much liquid is added to the first cell on each tick, 0 to 1
Attenuates and inverts the voltage at the FLOW input before it is added to the flow amount
A voltage added to the flow amount, scaled by the slider for FLOW, with 10V covering the whole range at the slider's full setting
Sets the volume a cell has to reach before it empties into the cell below and fires its gate, 0.001 to 10
Attenuates and inverts the voltage at the VISC input before it is added to the viscosity
A voltage added to the viscosity, scaled by the slider for VISC, with 10V covering the whole range at the slider's full setting
A rising edge runs one cycle of the flow, reading high above 2V and low below 0.1V
Eight channels, one per cell, carrying 10V on the ticks when that cell empties
Eight channels, one per cell, carrying the volume of liquid in that cell as 0-10V
Note — the square lights give the amount of liquid in each cell, brighter for a fuller cell

ChaosMaps.notes: The MAP switch is configured as "Map: tent or logistic", but 0 selects the logistic map and 1 the tent map; the readout on the panel names the one in use.
lines: Sequencer stepping one iteration of a chaotic map on each clock, with the logistic and tent maps to choose between
Chooses which map is iterated, logistic or tent, and the readout names the one that is set
Sets the map's coefficient, the knob's 0 to 1 covering 2 to 4 for the logistic map and 1 to 2 for the tent map
Attenuates and inverts the voltage at the R input before it is added to the coefficient
A voltage added to the coefficient, scaled by the slider for R, with 10V covering the knob's whole range at the slider's full setting
Returns the map to its starting value of 0.61834
A voltage above 0.1V returns the map to its starting value of 0.61834
A rising edge runs one iteration of the map, reading high above 2V and low below 0.1V
Carries 10V on the steps where the new value of the map is lower than the step before, and 0V otherwise
The current value of the map, 0-10V

Pluck.notes: The pluck angle is clamped to 0.9 on every sample, so the top of the DIR knob's range is unreachable. The output takes its channel count from the V/OCT input, while the voice loop runs one voice beyond that count.
lines: Polyphonic plucked string built on the Karplus-Strong algorithm, with control over damping, decay time, pluck angle, pluck position and pluck level
Plucks the string once on each press
A rising edge plucks the string, reading high above 2V and low below 0.1V
Sets the frequency of the string, 30 semitones either side of 261.63Hz
Sets the pitch of the string at a volt per octave, added to the FRQ knob, and the number of channels patched here is the number of strings that sound
Sets the damping of the string, 0 to 1, higher settings giving a duller tone and lower ones a brighter one
Attenuates and inverts the voltage at the DMP input before it is added to the damping
A voltage added to the damping, scaled by the slider for DMP, with 10V covering the whole range at the slider's full setting
Sets the angle of the pluck, smoothing the excitation more as it rises, and the value in use is held at 0.9 even where the knob reads 1
Attenuates and inverts the voltage at the DIR input before it is added to the pluck angle
A voltage added to the pluck angle, scaled by the slider for DIR, with 10V covering the whole range at the slider's full setting
Sets the time the string takes to fall by 60dB, 0.1 to 10 seconds
Attenuates and inverts the voltage at the DCY input before it is added to the decay time
A voltage added to the decay time at one second per volt, scaled by the slider for DCY
Sets where along the string the pluck happens, 0 at the bridge and 1 at the middle of the string
Attenuates and inverts the voltage at the POS input before it is added to the pluck position
A voltage added to the pluck position, scaled by the slider for POS, with 10V covering the whole range at the slider's full setting
Sets the strength of the pluck, 0 to 1, lower settings giving a softer and darker excitation
Attenuates and inverts the voltage at the LVL input before it is added to the pluck level
A voltage added to the pluck level, scaled by the slider for LVL, with 10V covering the whole range at the slider's full setting
The signal used to excite the string, halved on the way in and summed to one channel if it is polyphonic; white noise excites the string when nothing is patched here
The string, with one channel per channel patched into FRQ

MicroLooper.notes: The LENGTH knob's tooltip displays two to the power of the knob value, while the code plays a loop of half that many samples; the line describes the samples played.
lines: Recording sampler that plays one short loop out of a 32768-sample buffer, superseded by muLooper
While it is held, the signal being written is copied into the playback buffer each time the recording reaches the end of the buffer
A voltage above 0V copies the signal being written into the playback buffer each time the recording reaches the end of the buffer, and moves the RECORD button with it
Sets the length of the loop that plays, 128 to 16384 samples in powers of two, and the readout gives twice the number of samples actually played
Sets the loop length from a voltage, 0-1V covering 128 to 16384 samples, and overrides the LENGTH knob
Picks which part of the buffer plays, 0 at the start and 1 at the last loop-length piece of it, fading from one piece to the next in between
Picks which part of the buffer plays from a voltage of 0-1V, and overrides the SCAN knob
Sets the playback speed in samples per sample, -5 to 5, with negative values playing the loop backwards
Sets the playback speed from a voltage of -5V to 5V, one sample per sample per volt, and overrides the SPEED knob
Crossfades the output between the incoming signal and the loop, 0% for the incoming signal alone and 100% for the loop alone
Sets the dry and wet mix from a voltage of 0-1V, and overrides the WET knob
The signal written into the buffer, and the dry side of the WET mix
The loop, mixed with the incoming signal by WET

LFSR8.notes: The four CV weighting knobs have no names in the source; the panel labels the group V/OCT.
lines: Sequencer running an eight-bit linear feedback shift register, with a gate output for every register bit and four CV outputs summed from weighted bits, superseded by LFSR8 Poly
A rising edge shifts the register one place, reading high above 2V and low below 0.1V
Switches one feedback coefficient on or off; the register bits whose coefficient is on are combined to make the bit shifted in
A voltage above 0V switches that feedback coefficient on and a lower one switches it off, and the button for it moves with the voltage
Feeds the inverse of the combined bit back into the register, making it an XNOR register rather than an XOR one
A voltage above 0V makes the register feed back the inverted bit, and moves the not button with it
Sets how many of the eight register bits are used, 1 to 8
Carries 10V while that register bit is set and the clock is high, and 0V otherwise
Sets one of the four weights the CV outputs are summed from, 0 to 1; every set register bit adds one of the four weights, and each CV output starts the rotation of weights at a different knob
A voltage summed from the set register bits, each weighted by one of the four V/OCT knobs, reaching 8V with every bit set and every weight at maximum
Note — the round lights give the register bits, bright for a set bit and dim for a clear one

LFSR16.notes: configOutput is called twice for GATE1_OUT_OUTPUT, so the sequence 1 jack carries the tooltip "Gate Sequence 2" and the sequence 2 jack has no tooltip at all. The column CV outputs come from an expression that compares bits rather than shifting them, so they are not a binary reading of the column.
lines: Sequencer running a sixteen-bit linear feedback shift register that can be split into two independently clocked registers, with the bits also read across a four by four grid, superseded by LFSR16 Poly
Switches one feedback coefficient on or off; the register bits whose coefficient is on are combined to make the bit shifted in
Makes the first register feed back the inverted bit, an XNOR rather than an XOR
Makes the second register feed back the inverted bit, an XNOR rather than an XOR
Sets how many of the sixteen bits belong to the first register, 0 to 16, the rest forming the second register
A rising edge shifts the first register one place, reading high above 2V and low below 0.1V
A rising edge shifts the second register one place, reading high above 2V and low below 0.1V
A voltage built from the four bits of one column of the grid, 0V to 1V, the four bits not being weighted as a plain binary number
The four bits of one row of the grid read as a binary number, 0V to 1V
Carries 10V when the four bits of one column of the grid hold an odd number of set bits, and 0V otherwise
Carries 10V when the four bits of one row of the grid hold an odd number of set bits, and 0V otherwise
Carries 10V while the lowest bit of the first register is set, despite the tooltip naming it sequence 2
Carries 10V while the lowest bit of the second register is set
Note — each square light gives one register bit, red in the first register and green in the second, and brighter where the bit is set
